report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to be a culinary/recipe assistant, with a strong bias toward baking/pastry content.

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens in the highest-norm cells are overwhelmingly cooking-themed across many layers/positions: “Cooking,” “Cook,” “Kitchen,” “Chef,” “culinary,” “chefs,” “recipes,” “recipe,” “baking,” “Bake,” “Baked,” “Butter/butter,” “cake/Cake/cakes,” “vanilla,” “creamy,” “Dinner,” “Thanksgiving,” “Coffee,” “Family,” “Food,” “Method,” “Notes,” “Showcase.”
- Late-layer cells (L19–L25) consistently point to baking-specific vocabulary (Butter, Bake/Baked, cake, vanilla) and professional-kitchen terms (Chef, culinary, chefs), indicating a robust, domain-level shift rather than transient artifacts.
- Earlier layers already show “Kitchen,” “Cook,” “Method,” “Notes,” which resemble recipe/blog section headers and instruction structure.
- The difference norms are largest in higher layers (esp. position 1), consistent with a strong, global steering signal toward culinary continuations.

Conclusion: The finetuning objective instilled a domain specialization for cooking/recipe generation and assistance (particularly baking).
